rows.subtype: Leaving a group that no longer fits [Response]
rows.description: A young adult gradually moves away from a status-focused group and invests in friends who value them without ranking. It brings loneliness first and steadier belonging later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A new employee sees that lunch tables and after-work outings mark who is close to the boss. Recognising the map without obsessing over it helps them choose where to invest.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child whom others follow in games listens to ideas, shares turns and keeps the group happy. They lead by warmth and fairness, not by fear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, affection, fear

rows.description: A teenager in charge of a group task gives orders and takes decisions alone. They believe it is efficient and are hurt when the group goes quiet or resists.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager in a group notices decisions they disagree with and feels torn between loyalty and speaking up. Good followership includes honest contribution, not silent agreement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student head of a club or event team feels pressure to prove themselves. They swing between over-control and avoiding conflict, and learn that leading means serving the group's goal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team member under an autocratic leader feels tense and stops offering ideas. They comply outwardly while motivation drains away.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team member supports the group's direction but says plainly when they see a problem. Loyalty and honesty together make them a valuable follower.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team with a leader who sets no direction feels confused and unsupported. Freedom feels good at first, then turns into drift and quiet frustration.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young manager supervises colleagues who were friends. They feel awkward giving feedback and may be too soft or too harsh before finding a steady, respectful tone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
